review.notes:
Chain starts at lineage v3 (LC5D-EN231, 2014-10-23), which the baseline implements (cdb text ratio 0.975, differing only by '1+' vs '1 or more'). Earlier transitions v0 (TDGS-EN042, 2008-09-02) -> v1 (DTP1-EN030, 2009-06-20) -> v2 (DT01-EN087, 2010-01-29) -> v3 are punctuation/PSCT only; v0 is the printing in force at the Edison snapshot and is behaviourally identical to v3. Trailing v4 -> v5 (BLAR-EN057, 2020-07-23) is GY / '1+' cosmetic. Secondary script differences that the erratum did not cause and that no source documents as an era ruling: the pre-errata spells its trigger condition inline (requires Goyo to be related to the battle and face-up) instead of aux.bdogcon (which instead checks STATUS_OPPO_BATTLE), and its target check calls bc:IsCanBeSpecialSummoned(e,0,tp,false,false) without the POS_FACEUP_DEFENSE argument the modern check passes. Recorded here rather than in the summary because they are implementation drift, not the documented behavioural difference.

Round 037 (2026-09-29). Checked against period rulings: the differences the functional transition claims were searched for in the Konami-hosted UDE card FAQ (2008-12), the 2005 UDE card rulings page, Konami's errata lists, rulebooks and per-set ruling documents, and the archived UDE judge-list threads Yugipedia points to (the transition's rulings_check; docs/research/text-only-errata-audit.md, Goyo Guardian). No period ruling in the corpus settles a claimed difference, so the functional call stands unchanged (`unresolved` at both snapshots); the search is recorded in the check. Verdicts: [event] d1 unresolved at Edison, unresolved at Tengu.

effective.basis: TCG release of the first printing carrying the errata'd text (DUSA-EN075, Duelist Saga) Independently corroborated by Konami's own errata announcement and the archived Forbidden & Limited List page carrying its effective date; the printing remains the anchor because it is when the text first became available in the TCG (the announcement and the F/L effective date differ by a few days).

corroboration.quote: An 'errata' is a correction to the text on a card. If a card has errata, you should always play the card as if it had the corrected text, even though your actual card might have older text.

event.historical_text: 1 Tuner + 1 or more non-Tuner monstersWhen this card destroys an opponent's monster by battle and sends it to the Graveyard: You can Special Summon that monster to your side of the field in Defense Position.
event.modern_text: 1 EARTH Tuner + 1 or more non-Tuner monstersWhen this card destroys an opponent's monster by battle and sends it to the Graveyard: You can Special Summon that monster to your field in Defense Position.
event.summary: Functional erratum: the Synchro Material requirement narrowed from '1 Tuner' to '1 EARTH Tuner'. The pre-errata script calls Synchro.AddProcedure(c,nil,1,1,Synchro.NonTuner(nil),1,99) with no Tuner filter, so any Tuner is legal material; the modern script passes an ATTRIBUTE_EARTH filter for the Tuner. The capture effect itself is unchanged by the erratum.

rulings_check.difference: Era: any Tuner is a legal Synchro Material ('1 Tuner + 1 or more non-Tuner monsters'); modern: the Tuner must be an EARTH Tuner.
